summary: Register lists a 100-ft Aermotor tower in Oktibbeha County, Miss.; a 2020 report called it unused, and a 2022 visit noted repairs.

facts.design: 100-ft Aermotor tower with a parallel staircase

events.note: County fire coordinator said the Maben-Sturgis Road tower 'has just been sitting there'; the county then had two standing towers
Register site visit on 3 July 2022; someone had recently replaced some missing boards
Amateur radio repeater listing (added 2022-05-15, last updated 2024-03-06) gives its site as the Maben Fire Tower; the listing does not say the equipment is on the lookout

evidence.quote: Someone has recently replaced some missing boards

evidence.supports: fire towers were the main means of locating fires
evidence.quote: fire towers were the primary means of pinpointing the exact location of a wildfire before technological advances put them out of use

evidence.supports: fire coordinator Kirk Rosenhan; towers watched for smoke and gave coordinates
evidence.quote: People stationed in the huts at the top of the towers would watch for smoke, and when two towers spotted the same fire, they gave the exact coordinates to authorities and sent them to put out the fire

evidence.supports: Kirk Rosenhan identified as county fire coordinator
evidence.quote: Oktibbeha County fire coordinator Kirk Rosenhan said

evidence.supports: forester Bill Kitchens; phasing out fire towers from late 1980s
evidence.quote: Kitchens estimates that MFC started “phasing out” fire towers as a tool in the late 1980s.

evidence.supports: 2020 article: Maben-Sturgis Road tower one of two standing in county
evidence.quote: The tower on Maben-Sturgis Road is one of two still standing in Oktibbeha County, and the other is on Highway 12 southwest of Starkville on the way to Longview.

evidence.supports: other county tower used as a radio tower
evidence.quote: The latter is being used as a radio tower

evidence.supports: Maben-Sturgis Road tower unused, sitting there
stairs removed from some towers statewide to deter climbing
evidence.quote: Kitchens said MFC removed the stairs from some towers statewide to keep people from climbing them.

evidence.supports: repeater site named Maben Fire Tower
evidence.quote: Maben • Maben Fire Tower • Oktibbeha County • Mississippi

corrections.why: The register gives N 33.499815° W 088.793285° for the Maben tower in Oktibbeha County. The record's OpenStreetMap point is about 26 km farther west. Check the site before changing it.

sources.title: Area fire towers hold sentimental value long after falling out of use

notes_for_editor: Register coordinates are about 26 km east of the record's OSM point (register -88.793285, record -89.070897); correction proposed, not applied. Register elevation is 604 ft (184 m); record has 172 m from OSM. Record county is null; register and story say Oktibbeha County. The register names no road, so the 2020 article's Maben-Sturgis Road tower may not be this one; the two sources are linked by name only. The repeater listing's site name does not say the equipment is on the lookout. height_m not set because the register's 100 ft does not say whether it is to the cab floor. Access not established; no source says whether the public may climb it.
